title: 01. Foundations: Day 1 — Introduction to Pydantic AI and Your First Typed Agent

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Welcome to Day 1. Today you install Pydantic AI, wire up an API key, and build a typed agent that classifies text into a Pydantic model. By the end of this file you'll understand the `Agent` class, `system_prompt`, `model`, and `result_type` — the four primitives that 90% of Pydantic AI code uses.

sections.title: Why Pydantic AI?
sections.body:
If you've already used the raw OpenAI SDK, you know the routine: build a list of messages, call `client.chat.completions.create(...)`, then `json.loads()` the response and pray the model returned valid JSON. Pydantic AI removes that prayer step. You declare a Pydantic model, set it as `result_type`, and the framework guarantees the agent's output is validated against that schema — retrying automatically if the model returns malformed data.

Compared to **LangChain**, Pydantic AI is smaller and more opinionated about type safety. LangChain shines for composing long chains of runnables and plugging in dozens of integrations; Pydantic AI shines when you want one agent with strong input/output contracts, easy testing, and clean dependency injection. The mental model is also simpler: one `Agent` object, decorated tools, typed deps — that's it.

A final reason to learn it: the same team behind Pydantic maintains Pydantic AI, so the type-safety story is first-class. Validators, retries, and structured outputs are not bolted on — they are the foundation.

sections.title: Installation
sections.body:
```bash
pip install pydantic-ai
```

That single install pulls in `pydantic` (v2), `httpx`, `typing-extensions`, and provider-specific helpers. If you plan to use Anthropic, OpenAI, or others, you can install their SDKs explicitly to pin versions:

```bash
pip install pydantic-ai openai anthropic
```

For local models via Ollama, no extra SDK is required — Pydantic AI talks to Ollama over HTTP.

sections.title: API Key Setup with .env
sections.body:
Create a project folder and add a `.env` file:

```bash
mkdir day01 && cd day01
echo 'OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-real-key-here' > .env
```

Then in every script, load the env file before importing Pydantic AI:

```python
# load_env.py
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()  # reads .env in cwd and exports vars into os.environ

import os
print("Key loaded?", bool(os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")))
```

Pydantic AI reads keys directly from `os.environ` when you instantiate a model, so `load_dotenv()` at the top of your entry script is the only setup you need.

sections.title: Core Concepts: Agent, system_prompt, model, result_type
sections.body:
The **`Agent`** class is the central object. You construct it once, then call `.run()` (sync) or `.run_sync()` / `.run()` (async) to execute it. Four arguments matter most on construction:

- **`model`** — which LLM to use. Can be a string like `"openai:gpt-4o-mini"`, a `Model` instance, or omitted (then Pydantic AI infers from env vars).
- **`system_prompt`** — a string (or callable returning a string) that sets the agent's behavior.
- **`result_type`** — the Pydantic type the agent must return. Defaults to `str`.
- **`deps_type`** — optional typed dependency object made available to tools (covered Day 3 & 4).

Here's the smallest possible typed agent:

```python
# smallest_agent.py
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()

from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Greeting(BaseModel):
    text: str
    enthusiastic: bool

agent = Agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt="You are a greeter. Always be enthusiastic.",
    result_type=Greeting,
)

result = agent.run_sync("Say hi to Sam.")
print(result.data)              # Greeting(text='Hey Sam!', enthusiastic=True)
print(result.data.text)         # Hey Sam!
print(result.usage())           # Usage(requests=1, request_tokens=..., response_tokens=...)
```

Notice: `result.data` is a fully validated `Greeting` instance — not a string, not a dict. That's the whole pitch of Pydantic AI in one line.

sections.title: First Real Example: Task Classifier Agent
sections.body:
Now build something useful. The agent reads a user message and classifies it as `Work`, `Personal`, or `Urgent` using a Pydantic `result_type`.

```python
# classifier.py
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from typing import Literal

# 1. Define the structured output schema
class Classification(BaseModel):
    category: Literal["Work", "Personal", "Urgent"] = Field(
        ..., description="The classification bucket for this message."
    )
    reason: str = Field(..., description="One-sentence explanation of the choice.")

# 2. Build the agent
classifier = Agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt=(
        "You classify short user messages into Work, Personal, or Urgent. "
        "Urgent means time-sensitive and important. Work means professional. "
        "Personal means friends, family, hobbies."
    ),
    result_type=Classification,
)

# 3. Run it
def classify(message: str) -> Classification:
    result = classifier.run_sync(message)
    return result.data

if __name__ == "__main__":
    samples = [
        "Hey can you pick up milk on the way home?",
        "The prod database is down, customers are seeing 500s!",
        "Please review the Q3 roadmap doc by EOD.",
    ]
    for s in samples:
        out = classify(s)
        print(f"[{out.category:9}] {s}")
        print(f"           reason: {out.reason}\n")
```

### Line-by-line walkthrough

1. **`from typing import Literal`** — `Literal["Work", "Personal", "Urgent"]` constrains `category` to exactly three values. The LLM's JSON schema will list these as an `enum`, which strongly guides generation.
2. **`Field(..., description=...)`** — the description is sent to the model in the JSON schema. Treat it like a mini system-prompt for that field.
3. **`classifier = Agent(model=..., system_prompt=..., result_type=Classification)`** — one object, fully configured.
4. **`classifier.run_sync(message)`** — the synchronous entry point. Returns a `RunResult` whose `.data` attribute holds the validated `Classification`.
5. **`result.usage()`** — token usage. Useful for cost tracking and tests.

### How to run

```bash
python classifier.py
```

Expected output (categories may match exactly; reasons vary):

```
[Personal ] Hey can you pick up milk on the way home?
           reason: Family errand, not work-related, not time-critical.

[Urgent  ] The prod database is down, customers are seeing 500s!
           reason: Production outage directly affects customers.

[Work    ] Please review the Q3 roadmap doc by EOD.
           reason: Professional task with a same-day deadline.
```

sections.title: Switching Models
sections.body:
Pydantic AI supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, and any LiteLLM provider. The cleanest way is the colon-prefixed model string:

```python
# OpenAI (default)
Agent(model="openai:gpt-4o-mini", ...)

# Anthropic Claude
Agent(model="anthropic:claude-3-5-sonnet-latest", ...)

# Ollama (local — no API key needed)
Agent(model="ollama:llama3.1", ...)
```

For Ollama, start the server first:

```bash
ollama pull llama3.1
ollama serve   # in another terminal
```

Then run any script — no `.env` key needed. The same `classifier.py` works unchanged if you swap the `model=` line.

You can also let Pydantic AI infer the provider from environment variables. If only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, this works:

```python
agent = Agent(model="claude-3-5-sonnet-latest", result_type=Classification)
```

We'll cover the `Model` class and explicit instantiation in Day 2.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
- **Missing API key.** If you forget `load_dotenv()` or set the wrong env var name (e.g., `OPENAI_KEY` instead of `OPENAI_API_KEY`), you'll get an `AuthenticationError` from the provider at runtime, not at import. Always print `bool(os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"))` once during setup to confirm.
- **Model name typos.** `"openai:gpt4o-mini"` (missing hyphen) silently fails. Provider strings are case- and punctuation-sensitive. Copy names from the provider's model list.
- **`result_type` not a Pydantic model.** If you pass `result_type=dict` or a `dataclass`, the agent will fail to build a JSON schema. Always subclass `BaseModel`. Plain types like `str`, `int`, `bool`, `list[str]` are also allowed.
- **Async vs sync confusion.** `Agent.run()` is a coroutine — you must `await` it inside an `async` function. If you're in a plain script with no event loop, use `agent.run_sync(...)` instead. Mixing them (calling `run()` without `await`) gives you a coroutine object, not a result.
- **Forgetting `result.data`.** `result` itself is a `RunResult`, not your model. Always access `.data` (or `.new_messages()` for the raw message history).
